# drawbridge — social media domains
#
# Curated and pinned by SHA-256 in dist/policy.json, unlike the large upstream
# lists which rotate daily. Entries cover the parent domain only; matching is
# suffix-based, so `facebook.com` also blocks `m.facebook.com`.
#
# YouTube is blocked outright here. The safe-search rewriting in DnsFilter still
# maps youtube.com to restrictmoderate.youtube.com, but blocking is checked first,
# so the redirect only takes effect if YouTube stops being blocked.
#
# As of policy 43 that is a switch rather than an edit: the "Allow YouTube (16+)"
# option puts these hosts in allowed_domains, allow beats block, and the redirect
# wakes up on its own. Restricted Mode therefore arrives with YouTube rather than
# needing anything else -- and it arrives at the DNS layer, where nothing inside
# the app or the site can reach it.

# YouTube — all of it, including Kids, TV, Music, Studio and embeds.
# Matching is suffix-based, so youtube.com already covers m., music., tv.,
# kids. and studio.youtube.com; only separate registrable domains and the
# specific googleapis hosts need listing.
youtube.com
youtu.be
youtubekids.com
youtube-nocookie.com
ytimg.com
googlevideo.com
yt3.ggpht.com
youtubei.googleapis.com
youtube.googleapis.com

threads.net
threads.com

# TikTok — the app talks to ByteDance, not to tiktok.com
#
# Added 2026-08-18 after TikTok Lite served video on an alpha phone where the six
# tiktok-branded entries below were already blocked. The Lite build reaches the
# same backend under the parent company's own names, so blocking the brand blocks
# the website and leaves the app working: api.snssdk.com for the feed,
# ibytedtos/byteimg/pstatp for the media. Instagram Lite showed nothing on the
# same phone, which is the control — Meta serves its Lite build from the same
# instagram.com and fbcdn.net the full app uses.
tiktok.com
tiktokv.com
tiktokcdn.com
tiktokcdn-us.com
byteoversea.com
musical.ly
douyin.com

byted.org
bytedns.net
